name: APT / ADAPT
full_name: Advanced Particle-astrophysics Telescope / Antarctic Demonstrator for APT
summary: APT is proposed for a space orbit; its named demonstrator ADAPT is a long-duration balloon payload from McMurdo, Antarctica. APT and ADAPT are grouped as one series; ADAPT and AdEPT are different instruments.
detection_principle: An imaging scintillation calorimeter and fiber / silicon tracking combine Compton and pair-conversion imaging. Space-based APT aims to test dark-matter gamma rays with large acceptance; ADAPT validates technology and operation in a balloon environment.

sites.name: ADAPT balloon
sites.location: McMurdo long-duration balloon facility; planned 2026–2027 Antarctic season

status.label: Full APT remains a proposal. ADAPT is on the formal 2026–2027 Antarctic-season flight plan but had not launched by this dossier's cutoff date

key_parameters.name: ADAPT flight objective
key_parameters.value: About 30 days, planned; NASA scheduling spans December 2026 to January 2027

key_parameters.name: APT dark-matter research
key_parameters.value: Dwarf-galaxy gamma-ray sensitivity studies; ADAPT's short exposure is not long-duration APT observation

phases.name: ADAPT
phases.description: Integration and preparation for a 2026–2027 Antarctic technology-demonstration balloon flight

results.summary: Independent studies estimate that APT could test some thermal-relic models up to masses of several hundred GeV; results depend on targets, backgrounds and design assumptions.

science_scope: Searches cosmic gamma-ray, antiparticle or neutrino spectra, directions and fluxes for indirect signatures of dark-matter annihilation, decay or related new physics. Conventional astrophysical sources and propagation can produce similar signals, requiring background modeling; design sensitivity is not a measured limit or discovery.
